character: Europe's highest ski resort. Snow-sure, lively, purpose-built — 99% of slopes above 2,000m, six glaciers, long season from late November to early May.
description: Val Thorens is the highest ski resort in Europe at 2,300m. It sits in a huge sun-trap cirque crowned with six glaciers at the head of the Belleville Valley. 99% of its slopes are above 2,000m, making it one of the most snow-reliable resorts in the Alps. The architecture is purpose-built but the skiing is world-class — direct access to the 600km Les Trois Vallées domain, lively apres (La Folie Douce, Malaysia Club, 40+ bars), and genuine ski-in/ski-out convenience.

weather_snow.snow_reliability_note: 99% of terrain above 2,000m. Six glaciers. Consistent snow from December through April.
weather_snow.typical_snowfall_note: Heavy snowfall from December to March. Spring skiing reliable through April.
weather_snow.weather_pattern: High alpine — can be cold and exposed. Treeless landscape means no sheltered spots. High winds can close lifts. When sun is out, stunning 360° panoramas.
weather_snow.sun_exposure: Sun-trap cirque — good sun when weather is clear. South-facing slopes catch morning sun.
weather_snow.weakness: Exposed position — high winds and heavy snowfall can force lift closures. Treeless, so no shelter on slopes.

villages.name: Val Thorens Centre
villages.character: Compact, pedestrianised, purpose-built resort at the head of the Belleville Valley. Ski-in/ski-out throughout — you can ski from your accommodation to the lifts. Lively apres scene with 40+ bars, two nightclubs. The architecture is functional 1970s but recent renovations have added luxury hotels (Le Coucou, Hotel Pashmina).
villages.architecture: Purpose-built 1970s with recent luxury additions (Le Coucou, Altapura)
villages.shopping: Galerie Caron complex — supermarket, shops, pharmacy, sports equipment, rental
villages.dining: 60+ restaurants. Range from piste-side to gourmet. Key: Chez Pépé Nicolas, La Pause de Pierrette, Le Caron 3200 (summit wine bar)
villages.apres: La Folie Douce (iconic), Bar 360, 40+ bars, Malaysia Club (Europe's highest nightclub)

spas_and_wellness: Le Coucou — Tata Harper spa, indoor/outdoor heated pool, 5-star hotel, Pierre Yovanovitch design
Altapura — Scandi-chic, ski-in/ski-out, outdoor deckchairs with mountain views
Hotel Pashmina — Les Explorateurs ★ Michelin restaurant, spa facilities
non_ski_activities.swimming: Large indoor swimming pool at Galerie Caron leisure centre
non_ski_activities.ice_skating: Ice skating rink (outdoor, in resort centre)
non_ski_activities.zip_line: Double zip line — two lines side-by-side, 65m above ground
non_ski_activities.toboggan: 6km toboggan run from top of Peclet gondola — epic descent, lit sections
non_ski_activities.paragliding: Tandem paragliding from Cime de Caron (3,230m)
non_ski_activities.dog_sledding: Multiple operators offering half-day and full-day excursions
non_ski_activities.snowshoeing: Guided and self-guided trails — marked itineraries from tourist office
non_ski_activities.ice_climbing: Guided ice climbing on natural icefalls in the Vanoise
non_ski_activities.cinema: Cinema in resort centre (some screenings in English)
non_ski_activities.fitness: Gym, fitness classes, squash courts at Galerie Caron leisure centre
non_ski_activities.events: Weekly concerts, DJ sets, Cime de Caron 3,200m wine bar experience

signature: Chez Pépé Nicolas — piste-side, Savoyard specialities, local producers
La Pause de Pierrette — Hotel Le Portillo, fresh produce, sunny south-facing terrace
Le Caron 3200 — wine bar at summit of Cime de Caron gondola (3,200m), 360° panoramas, book ahead
L'Alpin — traditional mountain restaurant, good value
dining_guide.mountain: Caron 3200 (summit), La Fruitière (Folie Douce area), Chez Pépé Nicolas (piste-side)

piste_guide.beginners: Nursery slopes at front of resort with covered conveyor belts (sheltered from wind). Green runs from Col de la Chambre. Dedicated beginner zones.
piste_guide.intermediates: Exceptional — 74% of terrain. Wide blues and reds across Cime de Caron, Rosael, Pointe de Thorens. Long cruise runs with stunning views.
piste_guide.advanced: Limited steep terrain locally — 12% black. Best advanced skiing is accessed via Orelle sector (Maurienne valley) or off-piste routes.
piste_guide.off_piste: World-class. Gebroulaz glacier towards Méribel/Pralognan, Maurienne side, Lac du Lou from Combe de Rosael, Vallée des Encombres. Guide essential.
piste_guide.snowpark: Fun park and advanced park — good for freestyle. Major snowparks on Méribel side for serious freestylers.
piste_guide.crowding: Busy in February and school holidays. Best skiing early morning and late afternoon. Orelle sector quieter.
piste_guide.longest_run: 12km from Cime de Caron down to resort
piste_guide.key_run: Caron — 3km black run, most difficult in the domain

apres_guide.iconic: La Folie Douce — live music, dancing on tables, starts 2pm slope-side. Europe's iconic afternoon apres.
apres_guide.bars: Bar 360 — mid-mountain, music until lifts close. 40+ bars in resort including Café Face, Le TONIC, Le Monde
apres_guide.clubs: Malaysia — Europe's highest nightclub, subterranean, live gigs, open until late
apres_guide.vibe: Lively and young — Val Thorens attracts a party crowd. More low-key than Les Arcs 1950, more fun than Courchevel 1850.

comparison.vs_courchevel: Younger, livelier, more casual. Less luxury, less expensive, better snow, more exposed.
comparison.vs_meribel: Higher, more snow-sure, livelier apres. Less charm, less tree-lined skiing.
comparison.vs_tignes: Comparable altitude and snow reliability. Tignes has glacier/summer skiing. VT has better apres.

honest_drawbacks: Exposed — treeless landscape, high winds can close lifts
Can feel claustrophobic in bad weather (cloud/fog traps in the cirque)
Limited advanced terrain within VT sector — need to go to Orelle or off-piste
Long transfer from Geneva (2.5 hrs) — further than Courchevel/Méribel
Altitude can affect sleep and energy for some visitors

practical_info.ski_school: ESF Val Thorens + several independent schools
practical_info.supermarket: Supermarket at Galerie Caron + smaller shops
practical_info.medical: Medical centre in resort. Hospital in Moûtiers (35km)
practical_info.parking: Underground parking (paid). Free parking at resort entrance (shuttle required)
